html:
A Spanish Franciscan friar who spent more than 60 years in New Spain and recorded the life, beliefs and language of the Aztecs in their own words. He is often called the first modern ethnographer.

He arrived in 1529, only eight years after the fall of Tenochtitlan. He learned Nahuatl and taught at the college of Santa Cruz de Tlatelolco, where young Nahua nobles studied Latin. With Nahua students and elders he gathered answers to questions about gods, rituals, medicine, plants, trade and history.

The result was the General History of the Things of New Spain, known as the Florentine Codex. It sets Nahuatl text beside Spanish, with some 2,000 pictures by Nahua artists. Book 12 gives a Nahua account of the Spanish conquest. Sahagún's aim was to help priests root out the old religion, and the Spanish crown later seized his papers, but his work became the main source on Aztec life.
sum: A Spanish Franciscan friar who spent more than 60 years in New Spain and recorded the life, beliefs and language of the Aztecs in their own words. He is often called the first modern ethnographer.
